newsitem.title: USA: UPS takes out newspaper ads calling for union vote.
newsitem.headline: UPS takes out newspaper ads calling for union vote.

text.p: United Parcel Service took out full-page advertisements in Tuesday's editions of national newspapers calling on the Teamsters union to put the company's latest contract offer to a vote.

"UPS has presented the union with a generous offer that responds in earnest to their concerns about wages, benefits, profit sharing, the creation of more full-time job opportunities, and a limit to subcontracting," the ad in Tuesday's Wall Street Journal said.
"If the Teamsters leaders are truly concerned with the best interests of their members, they will present this offer for a vote," the ad said.
The ads appear identically in national media, including The New York Times and The Washington Post.
UPS, which normally handles 12 million packages a day, also said in the ads that its part-time jobs -- one of the thorny issues in the 9-day-old strike talks -- were "great jobs with great benefits."

"Teamsters leaders call these 'throwaway' jobs. We disagree," he ad said. "In the time-critical package delivery business, part-time workers play an important role. These employees allow UPS to operate with the flexibility and speed to meet the urgency of our customers' needs."
UPS concludes its ads by calling on the union to "do the right thing."
A telephone call to the Teamsters seeking comment was not immediately returned.
